description: Set WARMDOWN_RATIO to 0.7 to test if a longer, smoother annealing period improves validation performance.
Set WARMUP_RATIO to 0.02 to provide a brief period for optimizer stabilization.
Increase DEPTH from 8 to 10 (model_dim 640, 5 heads of 128) to test whether the larger model wins under the fixed 300 s training budget despite fewer steps.
No edit proposed: the attention c_proj and MLP c_proj weights are already zero-initialized in init_weights, so the idea is already in place.

Replace the ReLU-squared MLP with a SwiGLU-style gated MLP whose hidden size is round(8/3 * n_embd) to a multiple of 64, keeping the parameter count close to the baseline, and initialise the new gate projection like the up projection.
Replace the linear warmdown logic with a cosine decay to allow for a smoother reduction in learning rate during the final phase of training.
Reduce TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE from 2^19 to 2^18 to more optimizer steps, which improves small models within the 300s budget.

issues: Diff changes one hyperparameter only: FINAL_LR_FRAC goes from 0.0 to 0.05. It does not touch the evaluation call, data, seed lines, the prepare.py import or the summary printing. No integrity problem.
No bug that would make the result meaningless. A final LR floor of 5% during the warmdown is a valid schedule change.
The numbers support the reject. The candidate scored 1.0919 against the incumbent's 1.0893 (lower is better), so it is 0.0026 worse.

z cannot be recomputed exactly because the noise standard deviation is not given. The reported z = -0.331 implies a noise SD of about 0.0026/0.331 ≈ 0.0079. Its sign agrees with the candidate being worse. With n=1 on each side, the evidence is weak either way, but it does not support accepting.

description: Set FINAL_LR_FRAC to 0.05 to ensure a non-zero learning rate at the end of the training budget.
Double gradient accumulation steps by setting TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE to 2^18 to improve step count fidelity on a token-starved small model.
Test DEPTH 6 (model_dim 384, 3 heads of 128) as a smaller model that gets more training tokens in the 300 s budget, with no other changes.

issues: No integrity problem found. The diff changes one line, DEPTH 8 -> 6. It does not touch the val_bpb measurement, the data, the seed lines, the prepare.py import or the evaluation and summary code.

No bug found that would make the result meaningless. A shallower model takes more optimizer steps in the fixed 300 s, so a lower val_bpb is plausible. A smaller model should also stay inside the time and VRAM limits.
The numbers support accepting the change. The candidate mean is (1.065 + 1.0656) / 2 = 1.0653, which is 0.0240 below the incumbent's 1.0893.

z could not be recomputed exactly. The incumbent has only 1 run, so it has no variance of its own, and the harness's noise model is not given. The reported z = 3.579 implies a standard error of about 0.0240 / 3.579 = 0.0067, which looks like a fixed noise floor. Using only the spread between the two candidate runs (sample std about 0.00042) would give a much larger z, so either way the improvement is well above noise.
Caveat: the incumbent's 1.0893 rests on a single run. A replicate of the incumbent would firm up the comparison, but this is not a reason to veto.

description: Test DEPTH 6 (model_dim 384, 3 heads of 128) as a smaller model that gets more training tokens in the 300 s budget, with no other changes.
Increase UNEMBEDDING_LR from 0.004 to 0.008 to test a higher learning rate for the language modeling head, which may improve val_bpb by putting more gradient signal into the head parameter.
Increase MATRIX_LR from 0.04 to 0.06 to test the hypothesis that a higher matrix update rate improves validation performance.
Set ASPECT_RATIO from 64 to 85 at DEPTH 6, which raises model_dim from 384 to 512 (4 heads); note this makes the model larger, not smaller as the spec's rationale claims.
Modify Muon momentum schedules to either start at 0.85 and ramp to 0.97 over 300 steps for non-scheduled runs, or start at 0.97 and decay if a schedule exists.

Add gradient-norm clipping (max norm 1.0) before the optimizer step so a single exploding gradient cannot push the weights into NaN; the loss was smooth at about 5.14 until step 1082, when it went non-finite and the fast-fail triggered.
Add gradient clipping to improve stability on small batches without changing effective training steps.
Reduce TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE to 2^17 to increase the number of optimizer steps per second, granting more small-batch updates.
Increase DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE to 32 with TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2^17 and reduce MATRIX_LR to 0.03 to compensate.

Set HEAD_DIM from 128 to 64 so the DEPTH 6 model (model_dim 384) uses 6 heads of dim 64 instead of 3 heads of dim 128; FA3 supports head_dim 64 and RoPE, QK-norm and value embeddings all work per head.
Abort: setting HEAD_DIM to 64 at DEPTH 6 is the same edit already tested in slot 18, which gave val_bpb 1.0694 (+0.0040 vs incumbent) and was rejected, so a new slot is not worth spending.
Set WARMDOWN_RATIO to 0.3 to spend more of the training budget at the peak learning rate.
